en.heading: 3 April: founding of the National Commission for Culture and the Arts
en.origin: The NCCA establishment anniversary marks the creation of the Philippines' principal public commission for supporting cultural and artistic development across the country's diverse communities. Republic Act No. 7356 was approved on 3 April 1992 and created the National Commission for Culture and the Arts together with a national endowment fund for cultural and artistic work. The statute recognizes culture as a human right and emphasizes pluralism and broad participation; its institutional anniversary is not the same origin as Museums and Galleries Month, created in 1991.

en.heading: 27 April: the National Artist distinction was created in 1972
en.origin: The National Artist establishment anniversary commemorates the creation of a state distinction for Filipinos who made exceptional contributions to arts and letters. It is the origin of an honor, not a personal artist birthday. Proclamation No. 1001, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 27 April 1972 upon the Cultural Center of the Philippines trustees' recommendation, created the category of Award and Decoration of National Artist. The proclamation also named painter Fernando Amorsolo the first National Artist. The award's founding history remains separate from commemorations of the births or deaths of later individual awardees.

en.heading: 22 March: the Philippine Army anniversary traces to the Tejeros Convention
en.origin: The Philippine Army traces its institutional lineage to the Revolutionary Army associated with the Tejeros Convention on 22 March 1897 in Cavite, amid the struggle against Spanish colonial domination. Proclamation No. 2325 of 14 December 1983 temporarily assigned the same 22 March date to the anniversary of the Armed Forces as a whole, although it had traditionally been associated with the Army. Proclamation No. 447 of 15 August 1989 restored 22 March to Philippine Army Day and assigned 21 December to the Armed Forces anniversary, reflecting the Defense Act of 1935. This is a documented legal-date correction, not a second army founding.

it.heading: 22 marzo: l'anniversario dell'Esercito filippino risale a Tejeros
it.origin: L'Esercito filippino riconduce le proprie origini all'Armata rivoluzionaria collegata alla Convenzione di Tejeros del 22 marzo 1897 a Cavite, durante la lotta contro il dominio spagnolo. La Proclamazione n. 2325 del 14 dicembre 1983 attribuì temporaneamente il 22 marzo all'anniversario di tutte le Forze armate, benché fosse già associato all'Esercito. La Proclamazione n. 447 del 15 agosto 1989 restituì il 22 marzo all'Esercito e assegnò il 21 dicembre alle Forze armate, collegandolo alla legge sulla difesa del 1935. Non è una seconda fondazione.

en.heading: 7 June: the Philippine Film Development Council was created by law
en.origin: The Film Development Council of the Philippines supports local filmmaking, cinema education, film festivals and the development of Filipino talent as part of national cultural and economic life. Republic Act No. 9167 was approved on 7 June 2002 and established the Film Development Council under the Office of the President, replacing the previous Film Development Foundation and Film Rating Board. The founding legislation provided for evaluation of local films, incentives to quality productions and participation in festivals and international markets. The council's legal founding must not be confused with Philippine cinema's older artistic beginnings.

en.heading: 29 August: the Jones Act and the House's longer Assembly history
en.origin: The House of Representatives traces a predecessor to the Philippine Assembly, whose first session was held on 16 October 1907. This earlier elected body predates the bicameral Congress created under the Jones Act. The United States Congress enacted the Philippine Autonomy Act, known as the Jones Act, on 29 August 1916. It established an all-Filipino bicameral legislature with a new Senate and House of Representatives. The new legislative structure held its inaugural sessions in October 1916. Treating 29 August as a legal-framework anniversary must not erase the House's 1907 predecessor or be confused with the separate Senate institutional history.

en.heading: 8 March: Philippine National Women's Day is a working special holiday
en.origin: Philippine National Women's Day highlights women's contributions to public life and work and creates opportunities for institutions to celebrate and discuss gender equality. The law encourages employers and public bodies to allow participation in workplace celebrations; it is distinct from the March Women’s Role in History Month proclaimed in 1988.

en.heading: 29 August: the Jones Act created the Philippine Senate
en.origin: The Philippine Senate was created as the upper chamber of the elected bicameral Philippine Legislature under the Jones Act of 29 August 1916, replacing the earlier appointed Philippine Commission. The National Historical Commission's Senate chamber marker says the Senate was inaugurated at the Intendencia Building in Intramuros, Manila on 16 October 1916. The founding law and first session thus fall on different dates. The Senate's institutional history also records interruptions and relocations through war, constitutional change and later legislatures. Its anniversary shares the Jones Act with the House but is a distinct chamber's founding story.

The institution evolved through reorganizations and new names during the twentieth century, including the Philippine Museum name adopted in 1905. Its current founding anniversary points to the 1901 museum's creation, not a later renaming.

en.heading: 25 November–12 December: why the Philippine campaign lasts 18 days
en.origin: The Philippine 18-Day Campaign to End Violence Against Women treats violence and exploitation as human-rights issues, encouraging prevention, victim protection and greater public understanding. Proclamation No. 1172, signed on 17 November 2006, established the annual period from 25 November to 12 December; it built on the earlier international 16-Day Campaign observed from 25 November to 10 December. The two extra days connect the campaign to 12 December, cited by the decree as the international anti-trafficking observance. The national 18-day period must not be collapsed into the original international 16-day schedule.

en.heading: August: a national month for the Filipino language
en.origin: Buwan ng Wikang Pambansa celebrates Filipino as a national language and invites schools, cultural groups and communities to reflect on language, communication and national identity. President Fidel Ramos signed Proclamation No. 1041 on 15 July 1997, establishing annual celebrations for the complete period 1–31 August, not a single national-language day. The proclamation points to earlier constitutional recognition of a national language and to 19 August, the birthday of former President Manuel Quezon, who is often called the Father of the National Language.

en.origin: Conflict Resolution Day encourages mediation, conciliation and other non-violent ways of handling disagreements in families, communities, institutions and workplaces rather than assuming every dispute must go to court. en.origin: The Day of Sanctity and Protection of Human Life is a Philippine civic observance framed around respect for life and family. It is not the same legal observance as an independent Children's Day entry on the same Sunday unless a separate, verifiable instrument is found, and it does not make that Sunday a regular national non-working holiday.

en.heading: 22–25 February: four days of EDSA People Power remembrance
en.origin: EDSA People Power Commemoration Week remembers the four days of demonstrations from 22 to 25 February 1986, when a broad non-violent public movement ended the authoritarian rule of Ferdinand Marcos and renewed Philippine democratic institutions. Executive Order No. 82 of 22 February 1999 created the EDSA People Power Commission to preserve and explain the legacy of that revolution. The government's commission was established years after the original 1986 events. Presidential Proclamation No. 1224, signed 30 January 2007, specifically designated 22–25 February of each year as the commemorative week and asked authorities, civil organizations and the public to participate. Its name 'week' does not turn four days into a seven-day period or make them automatically non-working.

en.origin: Filipino Food Month celebrates dishes, preparation techniques and food traditions as expressions of Philippine cultural heritage, not only as products of the restaurant industry. Proclamation No. 469, signed in April 2018, established April of every year as Buwan ng Kalutong Pilipino; it expressly links culinary traditions to the 2009 National Cultural Heritage Act's implementing rules. The proclamation assigns leadership to the Department of Agriculture and NCCA and invites government, schools and local communities to take part; it explicitly recognizes farmers and agricultural livelihoods.

en.heading: 24–30 November: the history of Philippine National Book Week
en.origin: National Book Week in the Philippines invites readers to explore books, public libraries and the value of reading and publishing. The celebration lasts seven days and is distinct from a single international book day. President Manuel Quezon issued Proclamation No. 109 on 19 November 1936, establishing 24–30 November of every year as the national period for books and reading. The legal period falls in November, not April's National Literature Month. Those observances both promote reading, but they have separate historical and legislative origins.

en.heading: November: Children's Month moved from October by a 2015 law
en.origin: National Children's Month supports the rights and wellbeing of Filipino children and brings public attention to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted on 20 November 1989. A 1993 proclamation had declared October National Children's Month. Republic Act No. 10661, approved on 29 May 2015, explicitly changed the recurring month to November and repealed the earlier proclamations. The law names social-welfare, youth and children's councils as leading agencies; the current November calendar must not be shown as if the October designation had never existed.

facts: El Mes de la Infancia fomenta derechos y bienestar de los niños filipinos y recuerda la Convención de la ONU sobre los Derechos del Niño de 20 de noviembre de 1989.

La ley encarga la coordinación a organismos de bienestar, juventud e infancia; la fecha actual no debe ocultar el periodo anterior de octubre.

en.heading: 1–7 July: Philippine National Culture Consciousness Week
en.origin: National Culture Consciousness Week highlights Philippine cultural heritage, arts, writing and the varied customs of its communities within a national conversation about shared identity. Proclamation No. 1148 of 31 May 1973 designated 1–7 July of every year, referring to cultural preservation, national identity and the constitutional recognition of cultural communities. Memorandum Circular No. 644 of 25 June 1973 directed government offices and schools to organize cultural displays, exhibitions and educational visits during the first week.

en.heading: October: Indigenous Peoples Month has a separate 2009 origin
en.origin: National Indigenous Peoples Month celebrates the diverse cultures of Philippine indigenous peoples and calls for protection of their rights, traditions and participation in public life. Proclamation No. 1906 of 5 October 2009 established the whole month of October, building on the 1997 Indigenous Peoples Rights Act and an October 29 Thanksgiving Day previously recognized in 2003. The NCCA's Subcommission on Cultural Communities and Traditional Arts was assigned a leading role; month-long celebration and single-day Thanksgiving remain different legal observances.

en.heading: April: Philippine literature across many languages
en.origin: National Literature Month, also called Buwan ng Panitikang Filipino, highlights writing and storytelling in the Philippines' different languages and the ways books carry history and collective memory. President Benigno Aquino III issued Proclamation No. 968 on 10 February 2015 to designate April; the text mentions the April remembrance of poet Francisco Balagtas and other literary anniversaries. The NCCA and the Commission on the Filipino Language were designated as coordinating institutions; this national month is distinct from individual authors' birthdays and from UNESCO's World Book Day.

O presidente Benigno Aquino III assinou a Proclamação n.º 968 em 10 de fevereiro de 2015, escolhendo abril também pela memória do poeta Francisco Balagtas. en.heading: September: Peace Consciousness Month replaced an earlier week
en.origin: Peace Consciousness Month in the Philippines encourages understanding of nonviolence, reconciliation and the difficult process of addressing armed conflicts and their social causes. Proclamation No. 675 of 20 January 2004 declared every September the national month and superseded Proclamation No. 161 of 2002, which had prescribed a Peace Consciousness Week from 28 February to 6 March. The presidential text referred to several September peace milestones, including the 1996 agreement with the Moro National Liberation Front, and assigned coordination to the presidential peace-process office.
en.promoter: Office of the Presidential Adviser on the Peace Process are identified as leading or participating institutions in implementing the Philippine national observance and its public-awareness activities.
en.purpose: Build knowledge of peaceful conflict resolution and encourage informed participation in peace initiatives.

en.heading: November: Rice Awareness Month links food and public wellbeing
en.origin: National Rice Awareness Month in the Philippines focuses on the importance of rice for food, farming livelihoods and efforts to address poverty and malnutrition. President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo signed Proclamation No. 524 on 5 January 2004, aligning the national campaign with the UN's International Year of Rice in 2004 and designating November every year. The decree also notes the November anniversary of the Philippine Rice Research Institute, founded under Executive Order No. 1061 in 1985; this research-institution milestone is not the same event as the new annual month.
en.promoter: Department of Agriculture and Philippine Rice Research Institute are identified as leading or participating institutions in implementing the Philippine national observance and its public-awareness activities.
en.purpose: Promote awareness of rice production, food security, nutrition and the economic challenges faced by farmers.

La presidente Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo ha firmato la Proclamazione n. 524 il 5 gennaio 2004, collegando la campagna all'Anno internazionale del riso ONU del 2004 e scegliendo ogni novembre. Il decreto richiama anche l'anniversario di novembre del Philippine Rice Research Institute, fondato con l'Ordine esecutivo n. 1061 del 1985: la nascita dell'istituto non coincide con la giornata del 2004.

en.heading: December: National Volunteer Month and the bayanihan spirit
en.origin: National Volunteer Month celebrates Filipinos who give time, skills and resources to their neighbours, from local community projects to emergency and welfare initiatives. It draws on the bayanihan tradition of mutual aid. President Joseph Estrada signed Proclamation No. 55 on 5 December 1998, declaring December of every year National Volunteer Month under the Philippine National Volunteer Service Coordinating Agency. The recurring December proclamation is distinct from a separate May Volunteerism Month proclamation issued in 2009. These names are similar, but their periods and source texts must not be silently combined.
en.promoter: Philippine National Volunteer Service Coordinating Agency have the leading institutional role, where assigned in the original Philippine proclamation or legal record, for the observance's public activities.
en.purpose: Recognize volunteer work and strengthen civic participation and mutual aid in local communities.

en.heading: July: Philippine Nutrition Month replaced an earlier March week
en.origin: Nutrition Month in the Philippines supports public understanding of adequate diets, healthy eating and malnutrition prevention; it takes place throughout July rather than on one health-awareness day. Presidential Decree No. 491 of 25 June 1974 created the National Nutrition Council; section 7 explicitly designated July Nutrition Month and tasked the council with approving and coordinating activities. The decree states that the new month replaced the previously declared Nutrition Week in March, making the earlier week a documented predecessor, not an extra current month-long observance.
en.promoter: National Nutrition Council and associated health and education agencies are the institutions described in the historical state record as responsible for or associated with the observance.
en.purpose: Raise nutrition awareness and encourage practical prevention of diet-related health problems.

en.heading: April: Panagyaman Rice Festival — a 2004 presidential declaration
en.origin: Panagyaman is a Filipino thanksgiving expression associated with the rice harvest. The Panagyaman Rice Festival Month is described in the original presidential document as a national celebration of successful rice cultivation and the labour of small farmers. Proclamation No. 606, signed by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on 19 April 2004, declared 'the month of April' as Panagyaman Rice Festival. It referred to hybrid rice production and irrigation programmes as the context of that year's celebration. The signed proclamation does not explicitly say 'April of every year' or create a recurring national non-working holiday. The NCCA cultural calendar continues to index an April month, but annual statutory recurrence and ongoing government adoption require an independent official check.
en.promoter: Department of Agriculture, local rice farmers and community harvest-festival organizers are the relevant government and community institutions identified by presidential sources for implementing the commemorative cultural programme.

en.heading: November: Book Development Month moved from June in 2008
en.origin: Philippine Book Development Month supports book publishing, readership and cultural and educational access to printed and digital books. It is not identical to the seven-day National Book Week. Earlier year-specific June campaigns took place in 1997 and 1998. Proclamation No. 120 of 25 June 1999 then established June as an annual Book Development Month, linked to the 1995 Book Publishing Industry Development Act. Proclamation No. 1436 of 17 December 2007 moved the month from June to November starting in 2008, to improve student participation and align it with National Book Week on 24–30 November.

en.heading: January: Tropical Fabrics Month supports Philippine natural fibres
en.origin: Philippine Tropical Fabrics Month highlights locally grown or produced natural fibres and the textile industry's connection to agriculture, skilled work and cultural knowledge. The 2004 Tropical Fabrics Law (Republic Act No. 9242) provided a policy framework, while Proclamation No. 86 of 2010 called for a Philippine Tropical Fabrics Day on 24 January 2011. Proclamation No. 313, dated 12 January 2012, established the whole of January every year as Tropical Fabrics Month and tasked the Textile Research Institute with further research and engagement. It expanded an earlier single day.

en.heading: September: Rule of Law Month brings justice into schools
en.origin: Rule of Law Month in the Philippines encourages young people to learn how courts, rights and public institutions function and why lawful, fair processes matter. Proclamation No. 713 of 22 September 2004 declared every September Rule of Law Month and connected its educational purpose to the judiciary's programme of reform. The Department of Education was directed to coordinate school activities with the Supreme Court. The statutory month is an educational campaign, not an assertion that every September date is a national holiday.

en.heading: November: Traditional and Alternative Health Month
en.origin: Traditional and Alternative Health Month encourages public awareness of approaches to care discussed under Philippine health policy and the need to evaluate their safety, evidence and availability. en.heading: 21–27 March: UNESCO–ITI World Theatre Week in the Philippines
en.origin: The Philippine UNESCO–ITI World Theatre Week showcases dramatic performance, cultural diversity, education and the ability of live theatre to connect communities. The local week culminates on 27 March, the date associated with international World Theatre Day. Proclamation No. 1262, signed on 21 March 2007 by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, specifically designated 21–27 March 2007 and every year thereafter as the country's UNESCO–ITI World Theatre Week. The proclamation placed theatre activities under NCCA and the Philippine ITI Centre and referred to the 2006 Manila-hosted ITI World Congress. A later 2010 administrative order again refers to this theatre week. The national seven-day programme is distinct from the worldwide single day on 27 March.
en.promoter: National Commission for Culture and the Arts and the Philippine Centre of the International Theatre Institute are the relevant government and community institutions identified by presidential sources for implementing the commemorative cultural programme.
en.purpose: Encourage theatre education and cultural participation while keeping the Philippine seven-day week distinct from the global one-day observance.

La proclamazione affidò le attività a NCCA e ITI filippino e richiamò il congresso ITI ospitato a Manila nel 2006. Un ordine amministrativo del 2010 cita ancora la settimana, distinta dal solo 27 marzo mondiale.

en.heading: 18–24 October: how United Nations Week became annual in the Philippines
en.origin: United Nations Week in the Philippines recalls the United Nations' establishment in 1945 and invites discussion of international peace, human dignity, cooperation, development and the Philippines' participation as an original UN member. Proclamation No. 276 of 16 October 2002 declared 18–24 October 2002 a one-year Philippine United Nations Week, highlighting international themes including mountains, ecotourism and cultural heritage. Proclamation No. 483, signed 6 October 2003, explicitly repeated the period 18–24 October and added 'every year thereafter', appointing the Department of Foreign Affairs to lead. United Nations Day on 24 October is related but not identical to a seven-day Philippine week.
en.promoter: Department of Foreign Affairs and Philippine UN offices with government, local and civic organizations are the national authorities and civic organizations called upon in the original Philippine presidential proclamations to coordinate the described commemoration.
en.purpose: Promote UN principles and preserve the original 2002 one-off week versus the 2003 permanent national seven-day period.

it.heading: 18–24 ottobre: quando la Settimana ONU divenne annuale nelle Filippine
it.origin: La Settimana delle Nazioni Unite nelle Filippine ricorda la nascita dell'ONU nel 1945 e invita a riflettere su pace, dignità umana, cooperazione, sviluppo e partecipazione del paese come membro fondatore. La Proclamazione n. 276 del 16 ottobre 2002 stabilì il 18–24 ottobre 2002 per la settimana ONU, con temi legati a montagne, ecoturismo e patrimonio culturale, riferiti a quell'anno. La Proclamazione n. 483 del 6 ottobre 2003 ribadì il 18–24 ottobre e aggiunse 'ogni anno successivo', affidando il coordinamento agli Affari esteri. Il 24 ottobre è la giornata ONU, non la stessa cosa della settimana nazionale.

en.heading: Second Sunday in January: the people honoured by Unknown Citizens' Day
en.origin: Unknown Citizens' Day recognizes ordinary Filipinos who contribute to the country through daily work, civic responsibility, kindness and service without receiving public fame or prestigious titles. Commonwealth Act No. 152, enacted without executive approval on 9 November 1936, declared the second Sunday of January every year Unknown Citizens' Day to honour the rank and file of patriotic Filipino citizens. The law's text praises people who quietly support national progress by fulfilling their obligations. Its legally defined second Sunday is movable and should not be presented as the birthday or death anniversary of a famous individual.

de.origin: Der Tag unbekannter Bürger würdigt gewöhnliche Philippiner, die durch Arbeit, Gemeinsinn und Hilfe zum Land beitragen, ohne öffentliche Anerkennung zu erhalten. en.heading: June: W.A.T.C.H. Month encourages punctuality and honesty
en.origin: W.A.T.C.H. means We Advocate Time Consciousness and Honesty. Proclamation No. 1782, signed 21 May 2009, declared June W.A.T.C.H. Month and identified JCI Senate Philippines alongside education agencies and universities as partners in the campaign. en.heading: March: Women’s Role in History Month and overlooked contributions
en.origin: Women's Role in History Month highlights the contributions of Filipino women across social classes, faiths and communities, including work in education, politics, social reform and voluntary organizations. Proclamation No. 227 of 17 March 1988 called for observance throughout March and explicitly cited House Resolution No. 20, which proposed the annual history focus. The National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women was designated secretariat; the month-long historical recognition is not identical to the separate March 8 National Women's Day established by law in 1990.

it.heading: Marzo: il ruolo delle donne nella storia filippina

La Proclamazione n. 227 del 17 marzo 1988 ha invitato a celebrare l'intero mese e richiamato la Risoluzione n. 20 della Camera, che proponeva l'iniziativa annuale. La Commissione nazionale sul ruolo delle donne fu designata segreteria; il mese storico non coincide con la distinta Giornata nazionale della donna dell'8 marzo, istituita per legge nel 1990.

en.heading: 17–23 September: Clean and Green Week joins a full Cleanup Month
en.origin: World Clean and Green Week in the Philippines encourages communities to reduce waste, recycle materials and restore waterways, helping people connect environmental protection with practical local action. Proclamation No. 244, signed 3 September 1993, designated September of each year National Clean-Up Month and simultaneously fixed 17–23 September every year as World Clean and Green Week. The decree connected the programme to the international Clean Up the World movement and Philippine activities begun in 1990; the specific week and month share the 1993 act but are not the same period or independent global origins.

it.origin: La Settimana Clean and Green nelle Filippine invita a ridurre i rifiuti, riciclare e recuperare i corsi d'acqua, collegando tutela ambientale e azioni locali. La Proclamazione n. 244 del 3 settembre 1993 stabilì settembre come Mese nazionale della pulizia e il 17–23 settembre di ogni anno come Settimana Clean and Green. Il decreto collega l'iniziativa al movimento internazionale Clean Up the World e alle attività filippine dal 1990. Settimana e mese condividono l'atto del 1993 ma hanno durate diverse.
